multi-agent-monitor.title: Multi-Agent E-commerce Price & Competitor Monitor
multi-agent-monitor.problem: Tracking competitor pricing by hand does not scale, and the tools that automate it hand you a number with no account of how they reached it — which makes the recommendation hard to trust and impossible to argue with.
multi-agent-monitor.solution: Four autonomous agents — Collector, Analyst, Strategist and Notifier — coordinated by a hand-written orchestrator. The agents never call each other: each reads and writes one shared cycle state, and only the orchestrator decides who runs when. The language model is used solely by the Strategist, where weighing a rival’s move against margin and stock is a genuine judgement call; the statistical work stays deterministic.
multi-agent-monitor.outcome: Every recommendation carries the events that triggered it, the economics it was weighed against, and whether a model or a rule engine produced it. Competitor data comes from a simulated market over a fictional catalogue — a deliberate choice rather than scraping real retailers. The live model path has not yet been exercised against a real API key, so the demo output is tagged heuristic, not llm.

ai-sales-assistant.title: AI Sales Assistant (demo)
ai-sales-assistant.problem: An online retail business took orders through direct messages, and every enquiry repeated the same manual sequence: work out which product the customer means, check stock, quote a price, confirm. Customers do not write like a search query — references arrive in whatever language and spelling they happen to use, often several products in one message — so exact-match lookup against a catalogue fails constantly.
ai-sales-assistant.solution: An n8n workflow that delegates language understanding to an AI agent with a structured output parser rather than to pattern matching. The agent returns strict, validated JSON, so everything downstream is ordinary deterministic logic over typed data. Variant matching handles both exact values and numeric ranges against a live spreadsheet catalogue.
ai-sales-assistant.outcome: Handles multi-product, multi-language messages in a single pass. This repository publishes one 16-node workflow — the conversation-understanding and catalogue-matching engine — extracted from a larger eight-workflow system. It was built and tested for a real e-commerce client engagement, is not currently deployed for that business, and is shared for engineering context only.

ai-customer-reply-assistant.title: AI Customer Reply Assistant
ai-customer-reply-assistant.problem: A small business owner without a support team cannot watch a chat inbox around the clock, and an unanswered message is a customer left waiting.
ai-customer-reply-assistant.solution: A 16-node n8n workflow that watches a Telegram inbox continuously, classifies each message’s intent — question, order, complaint, urgent or other — and sends a context-aware reply in the customer’s own language within seconds. Every conversation is logged to a Google Sheet, and an email alert reaches the owner only when a message is an order or urgent.
ai-customer-reply-assistant.outcome: Built to keep working when something breaks: the AI call retries up to three times, then still sends a polite fallback reply and still logs the message, flagged for review. Reply, log and alert run independently, so one failing step never blocks the others. It deploys without custom code — import the workflow, connect four accounts — and ships with a plain-language setup guide. Sold as a template on my own store.

gotrek.title: GoTrek — tourism app
gotrek.problem: Travellers had no single reliable place to browse a city’s stays, landmarks and activities alongside the trips they might take next; the information was scattered and out of date.
gotrek.solution: A Flutter application built as a final-year project by a team of four, where I was responsible for the UI/UX design and the frontend implementation. It was later refactored into a layered architecture: hardcoded lists inside widgets became typed models behind a repository layer, so introducing a real API is a change confined to one layer and the UI is untouched.
gotrek.outcome: A frontend-complete prototype: guest browsing, in-city search, a sortable stays list, a booking flow with an itemised breakdown, and favourites that persist on the device. The backend is specified but not built — the app reads from a local seeded catalogue, and the repository is explicit about what is and is not real.
